Hi Monica —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on so we can do a proper unit-econ stress test before the procurement review:

1) Goal: surface a per-feature cost & margin view so your product + finance teams can evaluate payback and pricing sensitivity.
2) Redwood asks (we can run scenarios once we have these):
   - Current monthly active users for the candidate feature (MAU or monthly active accounts)
   - Average calls per MAU / month to this feature (or per active session)
   - Average prompt tokens and average completion tokens per call (or an example payload)
   - Expected % of users who will be charged (free vs paid conversion)
   - Target CAC and desired payback window (months)

For framing, we'll produce a short table showing: $/1M tokens target, implied $/feature at your expected usage, CAC payback months at different price points, and margin vs inference costs (with quantization / batching recommendations).

I attached a short econ model (redwood_econ_model_v3.xlsx) with example assumptions; if you can share a simple export (careplus_usage_export.csv) with anonymized counts, we can plug in your numbers and return a 1-pager.

Proposed next steps:
- You share the usage export and any target pricing bands by EOD Mon (Jul 3).
- We run 3 scenarios (conservative / expected / optimistic) and circulate a 1-page summary + recommended runtime config (batching/quantization).
- Quick sync to review results (30m) — suggest Wed Jul 5 10:00am PT.

If procurement prefers a different cadence we can accommodate — just want to align the data format to speed analysis.

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Feature unit-economics deep-dive & next steps (payback, $/1M tokens)

Thanks for the data, Monica — this is perfect to get started. I ran a quick top-of-sheet sanity check against our model and flagged a couple of items for the Wed session so we can converge faster: 

Preliminary calculations (ballpark, using the numbers you provided):
- Tokens per call = 120 + 320 = 440 tokens
- Calls per paying MAU / month = 4 => tokens per paying MAU = 440 * 4 = 1,760 tokens/month
- At 12% conversion on 45k MAU => paying users = 5,400
- Total monthly tokens (paying cohort) = 5,400 * 1,760 = 9,504,000 tokens (~9.5M)
- At a target customer-facing $/1M tokens = $1,200 => gross monthly revenue from tokens = 9.504 * $1,200 = $11,404.80 (rounded)

Now the inference cost side (using Redwood sample configs):
- Baseline inference cost without heavy quantization/auto-batching: $0.65 / 1k tokens (example run cost) => monthly inference cost = 9,504k * $0.65/1k = $6,177.60
- With mild quantization + batching profiles we expect ~30% cost reduction => $4,324/month (example)

Implications:
- At $1,200 /1M tokens, margin after inference cost (conservative) = $11.4k - $6.2k = ~$5.2k/month (~46% gross margin on token revenue)
- With optimization (30% lower cost) => margin ~62% on token revenue
- CAC payback: CAC $40 / paying user * 5,400 paying users = $216k acquisition spend; monthly net margin (optimistic) ~ 0.62 * 11.4k = $7,068 => payback on CAC ~30 months at current scale — which misses the <=6 month target if token revenue alone funds acquisition.

Key levers to hit finance targets / payback <=6 months:
1) Increase price per 1M tokens (move toward $2,500 if product tolerates) or charge per-feature subscription.
2) Increase conversion (higher ARPU) or charge a per-call surcharge for premium results.
3) Reduce inference cost further through dedicated capacity + aggressive batching & quantization (additional ~30-50% upside).
4) Offset CAC by cross-sell/up-sell or allocate only partial CAC to this feature.

For Wed I suggest we:
- Walk through the model assumptions in redwood_econ_model_v3.xlsx (I'll bring a second tab with sensitivity runs).
- Run 3 scenarios live (price at $1,200 / $1,800 / $2,500 per 1M tokens) and show payback curves.
- Flag commercial options (tiered pricing, dedicated reserved capacity) and approximate impact on unit cost.

Monica — anything else you'd like us to stress-test on Wed? If you can indicate expected churn lift or LTV assumptions that finance uses, we can fold that into CAC allocation.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
